name: Litti Chokha
description: Whole-wheat dough balls stuffed with spiced sattu (roasted gram flour), roasted over charcoal or fire, served with chokha, a mash of roasted eggplant, tomato or potato with mustard oil. It is Bihar's best-known dish and a popular street food in towns and cities.
how_to_eat: Break the litti open, dip it in ghee and eat it with chokha.
how_to_order: Ask for a plate of 'litti chokha' at roadside stalls; say if you want it with ghee.

name: Champaran Meat (Ahuna)
description: Mutton marinated in mustard oil, ghee, garlic, onion, ginger and spices, cooked in an earthen handi sealed with dough over a slow wood fire. Also called ahuna, handi meat or batlohi, it comes from the Champaran region and is now served in cities across India.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice or roti, scooping up the thick gravy.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Champaran mutton' or 'ahuna mutton' at Bihari restaurants and dhabas.

name: Champaran Taash
description: Grilled mutton from Champaran, one of Bihar's named non-vegetarian specialities.
how_to_order: Ask for 'taash' at meat stalls and dhabas in the Champaran region.

name: Bihari Kebab
description: Traditionally mutton kebabs, eaten with roti, paratha or rice. Patna is known for its mutton kebabs and reshmi kebabs.
how_to_eat: Eat with roti or paratha and sliced onions.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Bihari kebab' or 'reshmi kebab' at kebab shops in Patna.

name: Sattu Paratha (Makuni)
description: Flatbread stuffed with spiced sattu (roasted gram flour), also called makuni. It is a hallmark of Bihari home cooking.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with pickle, curd or aloo bhujia.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sattu paratha' at Bihari eateries and breakfast stalls.

name: Dalpuri
description: Salted wheat-flour bread stuffed with fried, crushed gram lentils. It is a common Bihari bread.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with a vegetable curry or kheer.
how_to_order: Ask for 'dalpuri' at sweet shops and breakfast stalls.

name: Kadhi Bari
description: Fried besan dumplings (bari) simmered in a spiced yogurt and gram-flour gravy. It is a staple Bihari lunch dish.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed rice or puris.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kadhi bari' at Bihari thali restaurants.

name: Dahi Chura
description: Beaten rice (chura) eaten with curd and sugar or jaggery; in winter it may be served with spiced peas and onions. It is a simple, everyday Bihari meal.
how_to_eat: Mix the chura, curd and jaggery together and eat with your hand or a spoon.
how_to_order: Mostly home food; ask for 'dahi chura' at Bihari eateries, especially around Makar Sankranti.

name: Chana Ghugni
description: Black chickpeas sautéed in mustard oil with ground masala, onion and spices. It is an evening snack in most Bihari households, often with fried flattened rice.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with chura (flattened rice) or mudi (puffed rice).
how_to_order: Ask for 'ghugni chura' or 'ghugni mudi' at evening snack stalls.

name: Dal Pitha
description: Rice-flour dumplings filled with spiced lentil paste and steamed or fried. They are a common Bihari breakfast.
how_to_eat: Eat warm with chutney or pickle.
how_to_order: Mostly home-made; ask for 'dal pitha' at Bihari restaurants.

name: Bagiya
description: A steamed rice-flour dumpling filled with sweet chaku, vegetables or other fillings, a delicacy of the Maithil community. It is a key part of Diwali on the day of Laxmi Puja.
how_to_eat: Eat warm, as a festive snack.
how_to_order: Mostly home-made in Mithila homes around Diwali.

name: Singhada (Samosa)
description: The Bihari name for the samosa, a fried pastry with a spiced filling. It is also turned into singhada chaat with sweet chutney, curd and chura.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for 'singhada' at sweet shops and tea stalls.

name: Silao Khaja
description: A flaky sweet of 12 to 16 paper-thin layers of wheat-flour dough with ghee, cardamom and aniseed, fried and glazed with syrup, often compared to baklava. Silao in Nalanda district is famous for it, and Silao Khaja received a GI tag in 2018.
how_to_eat: Eat it dry and crisp; it shatters, so hold a plate under it.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Silao khaja' at shops in Silao on the Rajgir-Nalanda road.

name: Gaya Tilkut
description: A winter sweet of pounded sesame bound with jaggery or sugar, pressed into thin biscuit-like discs. Gaya is reputed to make the best, especially the tilkut of Dangra village, and it is eaten around Makar Sankranti.
how_to_eat: Eat as is; it is crunchy and keeps for days.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Gaya tilkut' by weight at sweet shops in winter.

name: Thekua
description: A hard fried biscuit of whole-wheat flour, jaggery and ghee, flavoured with aniseed. It is the main prasad of Chhath Puja and a common gift sweet.
how_to_eat: Eat as a snack with tea; it keeps for weeks.
how_to_order: Ask for 'thekua' at sweet shops, especially around Chhath.

name: Malpua
description: A fried pancake of maida, milk and mashed banana, soaked in sugar syrup. In Bihar it is often served with thick rabri and is closely tied to Holi.
how_to_eat: Eat warm, with rabri spooned over.
how_to_order: Ask for 'malpua rabri' at sweet shops.

name: Anarsa
description: A rice-flour and jaggery biscuit coated in poppy or sesame seeds and fried in ghee, especially associated with Gaya. It is made for Diwali and other festivals.
how_to_eat: Eat as is; the outside is crisp and the inside chewy.
how_to_order: Ask for 'gur anarsa' at sweet shops in Gaya.

name: Harnaut Balushahi
description: A fried, sugar-glazed flour pastry with a flaky, porous texture. Harnaut in Nalanda district is famous for it.
how_to_eat: Eat at room temperature.
how_to_order: Ask for 'balushahi' at sweet shops in Harnaut.

name: Maner Motichoor Ladoo
description: A ladoo of tiny fried gram-flour pearls bound in syrup. Maner, near Patna, is famous for it.
how_to_eat: Eat as is.
how_to_order: Ask for 'Maner ka laddu' at sweet shops in Maner.

name: Makhana Kheer
description: A lightly sweet, rich pudding of fox nuts (makhana) cooked in milk. Bihar grows about 90% of the world's fox nuts, and the Darbhanga area is famous for this kheer.
how_to_eat: Eat warm or chilled as dessert.
how_to_order: Ask for 'makhane ki kheer' at Bihari restaurants or sweet shops.

name: Rasia
description: A rice kheer sweetened with jaggery, made as a special offering for Chhath Puja.
how_to_eat: Eat warm, usually after the Chhath fast.
how_to_order: Mostly home-made for Chhath.

name: Kesaria Peda
description: A milk sweet (peda) of khoa and sugar; the town of Kesaria is famous for its version.
how_to_eat: Eat as is.
how_to_order: Ask for 'peda' at sweet shops in Kesaria.

name: Khurma
description: Strips of flour dough deep-fried and dipped in sugar syrup, which crystallises into a powdery coat; it is also called shakkarpara. It originated in Udwantnagar and Arrah in Bhojpur district.
how_to_eat: Eat as a sweet snack.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khurma' at sweet shops in Bhojpur district.

name: Belgrami
description: A milk-solid sweet made with sugar and ghee, less sweet than khaja. It comes from Udwantnagar between Arrah and Buxar.
how_to_eat: Eat as is.
how_to_order: Ask for 'belgrami' at sweet shops in Udwantnagar.

name: Parwal ki Mithai
description: Pointed gourd (parwal) scooped out, boiled in syrup and stuffed with sweetened khoya and dry fruit. It is a distinctive Bihari sweet.
how_to_eat: Eat chilled or at room temperature.
how_to_order: Ask for 'parwal mithai' at sweet shops.

name: Chandrakala (Pedakiya)
description: A crisp gujia-like shell stuffed with sweetened khoya, coconut, cardamom and dry fruits, dipped in sugar syrup.
how_to_eat: Eat as is.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chandrakala' or 'pedakiya' at sweet shops, especially at festivals.

name: Laung Latika
description: A crisp pastry with a sweet filling, sealed with a clove in the centre and dipped in sugar syrup. It is a winter festival sweet sold at well-known shops around Patna.
how_to_eat: Remove the clove before eating if you prefer.
how_to_order: Ask for 'laung latika' at Patna sweet shops.

name: Kala Jamun
description: Dark, deep-fried milk-solid balls soaked in syrup, a darker relative of gulab jamun. Munger, Bhagalpur and Banka are known for it.
how_to_eat: Eat warm with a little syrup.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kala jamun' at sweet shops.

name: Lai
description: Discs of ram dana (amaranth seeds), puffed rice or beaten rice bound with khoya or jaggery syrup. Gaya lai and Barh's khubi ki lai are well-known varieties.
how_to_eat: Eat as a sweet snack.
how_to_order: Ask for 'lai' at sweet shops in Gaya or Barh.

name: Naivedyam (Mahavir Mandir)
description: A ball-shaped sweet of besan, sugar, cashew, raisin, cardamom and saffron cooked in ghee, sold as prasad at the Hanuman (Mahavir) Mandir near Patna Junction.
how_to_eat: Eat as prasad; it is a soft ladoo.
how_to_order: Buy it at the counters of the Hanuman Mandir near Patna Railway Station.

name: Sattu Sharbat
description: A filling summer drink of sattu (roasted gram flour) mixed with water, often salted. It is valued as cooling and energising.
how_to_eat: Drink cold, stirring first since the sattu settles.
how_to_order: Ask for 'sattu sharbat' (namkeen or meetha) at street carts in summer.

name: Bel Sharbat
description: A cooling summer drink made from the pulp of wood apple (bel).
how_to_eat: Drink chilled.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bel sharbat' at juice carts in summer.

name: Mattha
description: Spiced buttermilk drunk as a cooler, often with meals.
how_to_eat: Drink chilled after a meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mattha' at eateries and dairy shops.
